issues.existing: carved relief panels on the wheel's rim segments
issues.observed: The carved relief panels sit on the wheel's spokes, in the field between the hub and the rim, not on the outer rim segments. I logged one on the upright spoke directly above the hub (a long S-curved serpentine form), one on the spoke to the viewer-right of the hub (a quadruped in profile), and one on the lower-right spoke.
issues.evidence: The outer rim is a separate heavy blocky band with no carving visible on it; each plaque lies along the length of a radial bar running inward to the hub, following the radial direction, and the topmost one clearly starts just above the hub and stops short of the rim.

uncertainObservations: I cannot count the wheel's spokes. The visible upper-right arc is evenly divided and the spacing suggests a regular division, but the left half is behind the figure and in shadow, so any total would be a guess.
The carving on the panel at the top of the wheel is a long curved S-shaped form; it reads as a serpent but I cannot confirm a head or scales.
The relief on the spoke to the viewer-right of the hub shows a quadruped with a long muzzle and upright ears in profile; I can see the silhouette but not enough detail to identify the animal.
The relief on the lower-right spoke is too eroded/dark for me to make out what it depicts.
The large dark circular form behind the wheel could be a second wheel, a gear, or an architectural oculus.
Whether the figure is pushing the wheel or holding onto it to stop it is not determinable from the pose alone; I only record that the arms are extended and the body is braced.
The figure's footwear is indistinct — boots, wraps, or bare feet are all possible.

issues.existing: carved relief panels on the wheel's rim segments
issues.observed: The carved creature reliefs sit on the wheel's SPOKES, not on its rim segments. Three broad wedge-shaped spoke panels between the hub and the rim carry the reliefs: a coiling S-shaped serpent on the panel at about 1 o'clock, a long-muzzled jackal- or dog-headed beast on the panel at about 3 o'clock, and a winged four-legged creature on the panel at about 5 o'clock. The outer rim itself is a plain double band of masonry blocks with no figurative carving.
issues.evidence: Hub and spoke area, roughly x=200-520 / y=250-560 in the 560x933 image. Enlarged 3x and brightened, the jackal relief is plainly bounded by the wedge-shaped spoke panel that springs from the hub and stops short of the rim; the rim band beyond it shows only block jointing.

uncertainObservations: The image is extremely dark and heavily grained; I brightened it several times and many areas still resolve to nothing. Several of my readings here are low-confidence.
The spoke count is not determinable — the lower-left sector of the wheel is occluded by the figure and by shadow.
The lower spoke creature reads as winged and four-legged; whether it is a griffin, a sphinx or a winged bull I cannot tell.
I cannot tell whether the figure is pushing the wheel to turn it or climbing onto it; both readings fit the pose.
Whether the big dark concentric arcs on the right are the wheel's cast shadow or a second wheel set further back is ambiguous; I lean to a cast shadow because the arcs track the rim's curvature.
The figure's face is never visible, so nothing can be said about expression, age or sex.
I could not find a clearly drawn cast shadow of the FIGURE himself to corroborate the light direction.
